subject: Bullying Prevention and Intervention Plan Revision
overview: The subcommittee reviewed recommended updates from legal counsel to the Bullying Prevention and Intervention Plan to ensure compliance with state law and improve administrative efficiency. The body decided to remove redundant sections, update definitions to include school staff, and clarify reporting and disciplinary procedures for students with disabilities.

items.title: Review of Legal Counsel Feedback
items.summary: Attorney Howard Greenspan provided a line-by-line review of the current plan to identify areas requiring legal compliance updates and administrative streamlining.

items.title: Compliance Requirements and Review Schedule
items.summary: The subcommittee affirmed the legal requirement for a biennial review of the plan and decided to maintain a two-year revision schedule rather than moving to an annual review.

items.title: Anonymous Reporting and False Accusations
items.summary: The subcommittee clarified that no disciplinary action will be taken against a student based solely on an anonymous report and discussed the mandatory educational component required for false accusations.

items.title: Reporting Stakeholders and Procedures
items.summary: Members debated who is eligible to file official bullying reports, noting that while the law focuses on student-on-student interactions, parents and staff frequently initiate the reporting process.

items.title: Documentation and Disciplinary Policy Integration
items.summary: The subcommittee decided to remove the requirement to document 'all' behavior incidents to avoid administrative overload and discussed linking to rather than duplicating existing disciplinary policies.

items.title: Deletion of Redundant and Outdated Language
items.summary: Several pages of redundant definitions, outdated 'startup' language from 2010, and the entire curriculum 'Scope and Sequence' section were struck from the document.

items.title: Special Education and Manifestation Determination
items.summary: The subcommittee clarified manifestation determination rules for students with IEPs or 504 plans and updated referral language for repeat offenders who may have unidentified disabilities.

items.title: Modification of Disciplinary Options and Appeals
items.summary: The body removed expulsion as a bullying penalty and struck references to a formal legal appeal process, though members requested a clear administrative pathway for parents to contact the superintendent regarding findings.

items.title: Updates to External Oversight and Privacy Rules
items.summary: The subcommittee updated references to the state's Problem Resolution System (PRS) and the federal Office of Civil Rights (OCR) while correcting language regarding the confidentiality of personal staff notes.
